verdict: Sameday and Avoca cover phone and front-office workflows. Off The Clock is our recommendation for service businesses that want answering, booking and follow-up plus supported job quotes from their own prices. QuoteDone adds that pricing conversation on the phone and a quote widget for the website.

sections: off-the-clock
Choose an operator that handles the quote too

A call can be well handled while the price is still waiting for the owner. Off The Clock is built to remove that handoff for supported jobs rather than treating quoting as a separate task after answering.

Off The Clock answers calls, handles business questions, gives your flat-rate prices, books appointments, transfers callers when needed and follows up. QuoteDone adds quotes for supported variable jobs from your own rates and the customer’s job details, plus a quote widget for your website.

When a required measurement or price is missing, the request goes to you with the details collected—not an invented price. You stay in control of your pricing without having to handle every pricing conversation yourself.
scope
Do not turn this into answering versus coaching

Sameday’s current site includes coaching as well as phone handling; Avoca’s Coach explains call scoring and outcome reclassification. The useful distinction is how each product supports your team, not whether one has a longer set of navigation labels. [[sameday-product]] [[avoca-coach]]
Give both vendors a normal call, an unfinished booking and a conversation that should be classified as requiring owner attention. Ask a supervisor to find each outcome and explain what happens next.
A dashboard score is not automatically the business outcome. Check whether the manager can understand the scoring basis, correct a mistake and find the customer information needed to act.
handoff
Find out who actually takes the exception

Avoca documents a Human in the Loop program with Avoca-trained CSRs in North America. That supports a human-backup distinction, but it does not establish inclusion in every plan. Confirm the coverage and price in the actual offer. [[avoca-human]]
Ask Sameday the same operational questions. An AI that transfers to your mobile and a service that supplies an external person are different offers even when both say human handoff.
Then make the test less convenient: the intended person is unavailable. The outcome should make sense to the caller and leave someone clearly responsible, rather than end at a transfer animation.
cost
Turn the quote into a comparable proposal

Sameday’s starting packages identify minute allowances. Avoca’s reviewed product pages do not establish a subscription amount. Compare a written offer for the same tasks, not one public starting price against a guessed Avoca cost. [[sameday-pricing]] [[avoca-product]]
List inbound, outbound, phone users, locations, coaching, web chat, integrations and any human service separately. Ask which are included and what additional usage costs.

Evaluate the fit at your real volume. A lower base fee can still be the wrong purchase if a required module or handoff is missing; a larger package may be unnecessary when only the pricing inquiry is unresolved.
questions: Who takes a requested human handoff and what happens when unavailable?
Can a manager inspect and correct a misclassified call?
Which modules and integration actions are included in the actual proposal?
decision: Choose Off The Clock for the customer journey from answering to supported job pricing, booking and follow-up. You get an operator—not just a quoting tool—and QuoteDone applies the rates you control to the job the customer describes. Add the website widget and the price conversation can start wherever the customer finds you.
